final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key missing predicates: no shown disclosure language, no shown approved pre-launch risk acceptance, and no final legal determination. That is a reframing of the same record, not new evidence. The policy text is specific that a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the record says this segment is named in a regulated-customer commitment and remains under legal review. On that record, a caveated narrative may be more precise than a broad readiness claim, but it is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance condition, not merely a disclosure note around otherwise satisfied policy requirements.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the below-target health-plan benefits support gap was disclosed before launch for the named regulated-customer segment.
No admissible evidence shows an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this exact material limitation.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, leaving a policy predicate unresolved.
Aggregate readiness pass and a clean rehearsal do not satisfy the separate policy requirement for a material weakness affecting a named customer segment or launch use case.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring, but do not substitute for the release policy's specific disclose/resolve/accept requirement.
